en.summary: Recent releases bring powerful new capabilities for managing database changes across more platforms and scenarios. Databricks Lakebase now has credential-free interactive sign-in support, while Snowflake and Databricks Lakebase are now available as distinct database types in Desktop. The platform has also expanded its enterprise capabilities: code review policies can now be configured directly in Desktop, the new Automated deployment page streamlines CI/CD integration in preview, and AI-powered change explanations help teams understand what migrations do. For teams managing complex deployments, snapshots are now saved automatically, and an MCP Server exposes development-time tools that AI agents can call.

highlights: Connect to Databricks Lakebase securely using interactive sign-in with no need to store credentials
Preserve the exact capitalization of Oracle schema names in deployment scripts for consistency with your database
New Flyway Report implementation is now enabled by default for better visibility into deployment activities
Keep Oracle schema name capitalization consistent in deployment scripts using the preserveIdentifierCase option
Configure Flyway Insights publishing directly from project settings for easier integration
AI-generated migration descriptions are now shorter to prevent Windows path length issues
Search for policies on the code review settings page to find what you need faster
Test pending migrations against your shadow database before deploying to production
Use 3-sided diff to compare your development database, shadow database, and schema model in a single operation
Snapshots are now saved automatically during deployment, enabling drift analysis and rollbacks without additional setup
Snowflake advanced capabilities support is now available in public preview
The Deploy tab automatically reloads migrations after changes elsewhere in the project
Flyway MCP adds a new Test Migrate tool to validate pending migrations against your shadow database before production deployment
Use 3-sided diff to compare your development database, schema model, and shadow database simultaneously for better change visibility
Snowflake Postgres is now supported as a distinct database type
Databricks connections now have dedicated configuration fields for clearer setup
Deployment overview table in dry run reports shows exactly what will be deployed before you deploy
Exclude specific rule sets when analyzing schema models to eliminate inapplicable rule violations
Deploy command now publishes deployment results to Flyway Pipelines when enabled
Object level history is now enabled by default for Enterprise edition as a preview feature
Alert shows automatically when there are upstream version control changes you haven't pulled
AI-powered 'Explain this change' button in object level history describes what each commit did to your schema
Comparison filters can now be configured for Databricks Lakebase projects using the same intuitive filter editor
Diff viewer shows current position (e.g. '2 of 5') when navigating between changes
Debug logs now show final configuration parameters and where each value originated for easier troubleshooting
Databricks Lakebase is now available as a distinct database type for clearer project configuration
Add ONLINE clause to Oracle index creation scripts for non-blocking index operations
CockroachDB is now provided as a standalone database module for better compatibility
New Automated deployment page is now available in public preview to streamline CI/CD integration
Flyway automatically uses your operating system proxy configuration, making proxy support work out of the box
Deploying to a non-empty database now offers to baseline it automatically and continue, eliminating manual workarounds
Databricks Lakebase is now supported as a PostgreSQL-derivative database type in public preview
Snapshot history is now supported on Databricks for better drift detection and analysis
Add ONLINE clause to Oracle index creation scripts for non-blocking operations
Flyway MCP server now available with development-time tools that AI agents can call for state-based and migration projects
Code review policies can now be configured directly in Flyway Desktop on the project settings screen
New 'disable-constraints-for-static-data' option for PostgreSQL simplifies loading test data without constraint violations
Databricks advanced capabilities support is now available in public preview
Docker provisioner keepAlive now reuses the build database container across Flyway commands for faster operations
Configure a custom folder for drift resolution scripts using check.driftResolutionFolder setting
Configure drift analysis folder location as an advanced parameter for easier resolution script management
Filters UI support for PostgreSQL projects enables filtering out objects during comparison to focus on what matters
Flyway now warns when offline permits are expiring within 30 days so you can renew them before losing access
Preview Oracle option adds existence checks to scripts, preventing errors from recreating objects that already exist

de.summary: Neue Versionen bieten leistungsstarke Funktionen zur Verwaltung von Datenbankänderungen auf mehr Plattformen und in verschiedenen Szenarien. Databricks Lakebase bietet jetzt Unterstützung für anmeldedatenfreie interaktive Anmeldung, während Snowflake und Databricks Lakebase jetzt als separate Datenbanktypen in Desktop verfügbar sind. Die Plattform hat auch ihre Enterprise-Funktionen erweitert: Code-Review-Richtlinien können jetzt direkt in Desktop konfiguriert werden, die neue Seite für automatisierte Bereitstellung vereinfacht die CI/CD-Integration in der Vorschau, und KI-gestützte Änderungserklärungen helfen Teams zu verstehen, was Migrationen bewirken. Für Teams, die komplexe Bereitstellungen verwalten, werden Snapshots jetzt automatisch gespeichert, und ein MCP Server stellt Entwicklungszeittools bereit, die KI-Agenten aufrufen können.
